classifications.label: Instrumental drift or environmental cycle with ~6–8 day period
Cross-instrument systematic bias or coupling; instruments are not independent
Calibration or readout artefact: instruments are not drifting but reporting in a way that aliases environmental or instrumental state onto reading values
Random noise with spurious patterns at small sample sizes; all correlations are statistical flukes
Environmental cycle ~6–8 days with opposite phase response in pendulum vs. resonator systems
Shared environmental forcing or measurement coupling, with propagation delays between lab and observatory

Readout or calibration artefact: instruments report a hidden state (e.g., reference drift, thermal expansion of measurement apparatus) aliased onto reading values, not physical drift of the measured quantity
Statistical flukes from multiple comparisons at small sample sizes; no real signal
Unobserved: measurement schedule or operator procedure correlated with environmental state, e.g., trials clustered by time of day or week, creating artefactual lag structure
Environmental cycle ~6–8 days with differential phase response between pendulum and resonator systems
Measurement schedule or operator procedure creates artefactual lag structure (trials clustered by time of day, week, or maintenance cycle)
Shared environmental forcing (atmospheric, electrical, or thermal propagation) coupling lab and observatory with 1–6 day propagation delay
Readout or calibration bias (thermal drift of electronics, mechanical expansion) produces artefactual autocorrelations, not real physical variation
Statistical flukes from multiple comparisons; no real signal, all correlations are noise
Residual: unobserved mechanism (e.g., instrumental resonance to seismic noise, feedback oscillation in electronics, unknown environmental driver with exotic phase structure)

Perfect correlation r=1.000 is a computational or data-processing artefact (e.g., subsample of trials with identical reporting, aliased time-series window, or offset-matching error in cross-correlation code).

Measurement schedule or operator procedure clusters trials by day-of-week, maintenance cycle, or local time-of-day, creating artefactual autocorrelations and lagged cross-correlations without real physical signal.

Environmental cycle (~6–8 days: temperature, humidity, or atmospheric pressure) with differential phase response between pendulum and resonator systems, couples instruments at 3–6 day propagation delay.
Shared reference or feedback pathway between pendulum_lab and resonator_obs (e.g., one uses output of the other as a calibration standard with 3-day reporting delay) produces the r=1.000 correlation.

Readout bias (thermal drift of electronics, mechanical expansion, or reference voltage variation on a 6–14 day cycle) creates artefactual autocorrelations and cross-correlations without real physical signal.
